subject: Price shield: multi-year commitment outline and ramp options
messages:
From: Emma Chen <emma.chen@finx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — pricing protection for 2027

Karthik,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for Redwood is up in Q1 2027 and finance is concerned about the projected token price increases we’re seeing across vendors. We’d like to explore a multi-year prepay that:
- Locks a blended unit rate for 24 months,
- Provides staged ramp credits if our usage grows above forecast, and
- Includes a modest discount on higher tiers to offset the prepay.

Attached is our latest usage forecast for 2025–2027 (usage_forecast.xlsx). High-level ask: can Redwood outline a proposal that balances a meaningful price shield with reasonable payment cadence for a mid-market customer?

Can you share options (1yr prepay, 2yr ladder, and committed but monthly payment) with the trade-offs? We’ll need this for our internal procurement review by Oct 8.

Thanks,
Emma Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships | FinX Corp
emma.chen@finx.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: usage_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@finx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — pricing protection for 2027

Emma — thanks for the forecast and the clear asks. High level we can propose 3 options that match the trade-offs you described:

Option A — 12-month prepay (simple, quicker approval)
- ~8% discount off list per-token rate
- Upfront payment for committed volume; overages billed at committed rate + 15%
- No ramp credits

Option B — 24-month blended lock (price shield)
- ~14% blended discount across 24 months
- Staged ramp credits: 10% credit for months where usage exceeds forecast by 20% (first 6 months), 5% thereafter up to contract cap
- Quarterly reconciliation + carry-forward bucket for unused credits

Option C — 24-month laddered prepay (preferred for growth customers)
- Front-loaded discounts (year 1: 12%, year 2: 10%)
- Cashflow-friendly: quarterly invoicing against committed buckets
- Built-in safeguard clause: if market unit prices fall >12% we offer one-time adjustment or conversion to usage-based at lower price

I’ve sketched these into a term sheet and a commitment schedule (commitment_schedule.csv) and dropped both into the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C2kProposal.

A few questions to help narrow:
- How comfortable is procurement with any form of upfront payment vs quarterly invoicing?
- Is FinX likely to exceed forecast aggressively (50%+), or do you expect more modest growth?

If you’d like, we can run through the options in a 30-min call this week and I’ll invite Monica (finance) and Marcus (revenue ops) to answer billing/contract questions.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: commitment_schedule.csv (CSV), term_sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet stub)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700

Karthik / Marcus — forwarding FinX thread. Quick notes from finance POV:
- Option B looks attractive for FinX’s ask but we need a clear ceiling on credits and an overage formula that protects margin. Recommend: 10% credit cap per 12-month period and overage billed at contracted committed rate + 20% (not 15%).
- For payment terms, procurement usually prefers quarterly invoicing against committed buckets; they rarely sign large upfront full prepay without legal escrow assurances.
- Add a price review clause at 12 months (anniversary) to allow both sides to reconcile market changes.

If we want this to close before Oct 8, we should present a single recommended option with a short term-sheet and a clear list of procurement asks. I can draft the legal-friendly clause language if Karthik confirms the commercial shape.

-Monica
Head of Finance, Revenue | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Emma Chen <emma.chen@finx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finx.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — pricing protection for 2027

Karthik/Monica — thanks for the quick options. Procurement confirmed they will not sign full upfront prepay without some vendor escrow or a third-party guarantee. They prefer quarterly invoicing against committed buckets (Option C-ish), but would accept a 24-month blended price if we can:
- Limit the credit pool to 12% of total committed value per year,
- Overages billed at committed rate + 10% (procurement is pushing back on higher markups), and
- A 12-month price review clause with mutual termination if market prices change materially (>15%).

Can Redwood produce a recommended term sheet reflecting those constraints? If you can get back to us with a DocuSign link for a signable term sheet, procurement will prioritize review.

Best,
Emma

Attachment: procurement_finx_notes.pdf (procurement summary)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@finx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — pricing protection for 2027

Emma — appreciate the clarity. Based on your procurement constraints and Monica’s guidance we recommend the following commercial (our recommended single option):

Recommended: 24-month laddered commitment with quarterly invoicing
- Blended discount: 13% weighted across 24 months
- Credit pool: capped at 12% of committed value per 12-month period; credits applied automatically to the next invoice quarter after reconciliation
- Overages: billed at committed rate + 12%
- Price review: 12-month anniversary review; if market unit prices decline >15% we will offer one-time adjustment or conversion to the lower market rate; if market prices increase, FinX keeps the locked blended rate
- Payment cadence: quarterly invoicing against committed buckets to meet procurement's preference; 30-day net payment terms
- Legal: escrow/guarantee language — propose third-party custodial escrow for prepayment funds if FinX requires (we can provide recommended vendors).

I’ve attached the final term sheet (term_sheet_v1.pdf) and a signable DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/RWD-3247-term-sheet. Please review and let me know if all key points are covered — if so, I’ll schedule the DocuSign and route to Legal for a quick review.

If procurement needs any small concessions to finish by Oct 8, call me directly and I’ll pull Marcus in.

Thanks and looking forward to closing this one for 2027,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
